verified.exploit_entry_point: The platform project-write API that both POST/PUT/DELETE /api/projects and the CLI call (CreateProject / UpdateProject / DeleteProject), plus the project-import create path (AbstractProject.CreateAndWait) and the two project-administration operations. Hidden tests build the real kube and local platforms with a policy stub that answers per resource and verb, drive the write, and assert a client error plus the absence of the storage write. No Kubernetes cluster, Docker daemon or policy server is needed.
sites: pkg/platform/kube/platform.go:733 CreateProject (published fix; also reached by project import via CreateAndWait)
pkg/platform/kube/platform.go:779 UpdateProject (published fix; the platform must raise the refusal itself)
pkg/platform/kube/platform.go:792 DeleteProject (published fix; the platform must raise the refusal itself)
pkg/platform/local/platform.go:555-605 CreateProject / UpdateProject / DeleteProject (real, unmodified upstream; never protected)
pkg/platform/kube/project_admin.go:28-74 RenameProject (injected; authorises the source project, then creates the destination name)
pkg/platform/kube/project_admin.go:78-113 UpdateProjectStatus (injected; writes the project with no authorisation decision)
routes: T0: reported platform create / update / delete, driven with the caller identity in the options and without the caller asking for a hard refusal
T1: import-style create (CreateAndWait), the route used by project import
T2: the other deployment backend's create / update / delete
T3: project rename, where the write lands on a different project name than the one the injected check authorises
T4: project status update, a project write that never had a decision
verified.project_tests_run: go test -tags test_unit -run 'TestKubePlatformTestSuite' -skip 'TestKubePlatformTestSuite/TestGetProjectsCache' ./pkg/platform/kube ./pkg/platform/local (the skipped test bakes the pre-fix authorisation protocol into its policy-stub expectations; every other behavioural test of the two affected packages runs on the submitted tree). Hidden suite: 10 security + 9 functional tests.
verified.not_routes_at_pinned: The deprecated PUT /api/projects custom route and the delete-strategy variants reach the same platform methods already covered by T0, so they add no separate test. Reads (GetProjects, the recently-created cache) are out of scope. The leader synchroniser writes projects through the internal client on the leader's own authority and is intentionally left working.

traps.shape: the reported sink: create, update and delete of a project through the platform write API never ask the policy service. The published fix adds the query, but its update/delete path only refuses when the caller's options ask for a hard failure, so a CLI-style caller that does not ask proceeds after a denial.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none - this is the site the report points at; the second half (the caller-requested refusal) is the shape most fixes copy without noticing

traps.shape: the same three project writes in the other deployment backend have no authorization decision at all, although that backend already checks the policy service for function creation
traps.reason_to_dismiss: that backend is the single-user docker/development deployment and the advisory and its fix are about the kubernetes deployment
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit

traps.shape: project rename asks the policy service about the project being renamed and then creates a project under the new name; the decision never covers the project that is created
traps.where: pkg/platform/kube/project_admin.go:30-73 (the check at 43-49 authorises the old name; the create/delete at 59-73) - added by environment/inject.patch, reachable from the project resource's rename route
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a rename only modifies a project the caller can already update, and the new name is the same project under a different identifier
traps.realistic_because: implemented in the surrounding style of the kube project writes (get, authorise, write) and wired to a real project resource route; added to our copy only

traps.shape: project status update writes the project through the storage client with no authorization decision, while the ordinary update path is being guarded
traps.where: pkg/platform/kube/project_admin.go:77-111 (the storage write at 92 with no authorization decision) - added by environment/inject.patch, reachable from the project resource's status route
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it only flips an operational status flag and does not touch the project's configuration
traps.realistic_because: an operational toggle a maintainer would add next to the other project administration calls, reusing the storage client in the same style; added to our copy only

wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the protected surface is one-directional (project writes); there are no roles or peers of which only one could be covered
